claims.text: Systematically varying individual-element percentages in HfNbTaTiZr will significantly alter its mechanical properties.
The change in mechanical properties will occur through modification of the alloy microstructure.
The initial HfNbTaTiZr alloy is a near-equiatomic multi-principal-element mixture.
Laser powder bed fusion with algorithmically varied feedstock ratios can produce the proposed composition series.
Individual-element percentages will be adjusted in 5–10% increments during deposition.
Mechanical testing will be performed in situ during layer-by-layer deposition.
Standard mechanical characterization will be performed after processing.
Changing composition will alter phase distributions.
Changing composition will alter grain-boundary characteristics.
Changing composition will alter lattice distortion.
Elemental-percentage variations influence solid-solution strengthening by changing lattice distortion and dislocation mobility.
Increasing Hf or Zr may enhance lattice strain fields.
Enhanced lattice strain fields may increase yield strength.
Enhanced lattice strain fields may reduce ductility.
Elements that heighten solid-solution effects should increase hardness.
The relevant baseline is near-equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr produced under processing conditions identical to those used for the modified alloys.
The prediction is intended to apply within approximately ±5–10% compositional variation from the equiatomic baseline.
Extreme composition deviations might cause phase separation or other phenomena outside the proposed approach.
Interactions among elements may create complex property trade-offs beyond a simple solid-solution-strengthening mechanism.
A lack of statistically significant and consistent mechanical-property changes relative to the baseline would falsify the hypothesis.
